segments.text: Most people spend years learning English, but when they sit for a job interview, they freeze.
They forget all the words.
Their heart beats fast. One of my students had this exact problem.
He was great at his job.
His English was okay, but he failed three interviews in a row. The surprising part, he didn't need to learn more grammar.
He didn't need to memorize a thousand new words.
He just changed one simple thing about how he prepared. In this video, I will show you exactly what that one thing is.
I will share the simple method step by step. This student wasn't a genius.
He was shy. He was busy.
His level was probably very similar to yours.
Simple,
practical, fast. Let's see how it works.
First, let me tell you a secret.
Nobody talks about this.
The secret is this.
In a job interview, the company is not looking for perfect English.
They are looking for a good person to work with.
They want someone who can solve problems.
They want someone who can work in a team.
They want someone who is friendly and easy to talk to. This is the most important thing.
So rule number
one is this.
Stop trying to be perfect.
When you try to be perfect, you speak slowly. You stop and start.
You get nervous.
And nervous energy is bad for an interview. Here is the thing. Imagine you are the interviewer. You ask a
question.

The person answers perfectly, but they look very scared. They use all the right grammar, but they seem cold and uncomfortable. Would you hire that person? Probably not. Now, imagine another person. They make one or two
small grammar mistakes, but they smile.
They are relaxed.
They explain their ideas clearly. You enjoy talking to them. Who would you hire? Most people will choose the second person. So, that is our first step. Be relaxed.
Be friendly. Your goal is to have a
conversation, not to pass an English test.
Now, how do you prepare for this conversation? The second point is very practical. Most people prepare for an interview by memorizing long answers.
They memorize a speech about their experience. This is a huge mistake. Why?

Because if you memorize a speech, you sound like a robot. And if the interviewer asks a different question, you get confused and panic. Here is what you should do instead. You should prepare stories, small stories about
your work experience. You don't need to memorize a whole paragraph.
Just write down a few simple ideas. Let me give you an example. Imagine the interviewer asks, "Tell me about a time you solved a problem at work." Instead of having a
long speech, you just have a story in your head.
The story can be just three steps.
What was the problem?
Our internet was down for 2 hours.
What did
you do?
I called the IT team. I restarted the computers.
What was the result?
We solved it in 20 minutes.
My boss was happy. That is it.
Simple,
short.
You can use this story for many different questions.
What do you do in an emergency?
You can use the same story.
What is your biggest strength?
You can say, I don't panic when there is a problem.
For example, once the internet was down. So your homework is to write down three to five stories.
One about a time you solved a problem.
One
about a time you worked in a team.
One about your biggest achievement. That is all you need.
Knowing your stories makes you feel confident. That already helps a lot. But the next point is where most
learners make a huge mistake.
Let's talk about the hardest question. You know the one the interviewer asks.
Tell me about yourself.
This is the most common question and most people don't know how
to answer it. They start from their childhood. I was born in 1990. I have a brother.
I like to read books.
That is not what the interviewer wants. Your answer should be about your professional life. It should be like a trailer for a
movie. When you see a trailer for a movie, you get the main idea. You see the best part. Your answer should be the trailer for your professional life. Here is the formula. who you are now.
I am a marketing specialist. What you do? I
help companies sell their products online. Why you like it?
I enjoy finding new ways to reach customers. Your goal?
I want to bring my ideas to a bigger company like yours. That is it.
Short, simple, and professional. Not talk about your family, your hobbies, or your personal life. Keep it workrelated. This is the best way to make a strong first
impression. It sounds simple, right?
Well, the next tip is the real secret of successful interviews.
Here is something interesting.
Most learners think the interview is about them, but actually the interview is about them, the
company.
So, the best questions to ask are questions about the company.
You must ask questions.
If you have no questions, you seem bored or not interested.
Let me tell you a secret.
You can prepare two or three simple questions before the interview.
You can write them down and bring them with you.
This shows that you are smart and you care.
Here are the best questions to ask.
What is a typical day like in this job?
What do you enjoy most about working here?
What are the biggest
challenges for this position? These questions are simple.
They make the interviewer talk about themselves.
People love to talk about themselves.
When the interviewer is talking, they are happy.
It makes the conversation feel positive.
Also, it gives you time to relax and listen.
Listening is just as important as speaking.
When you ask
good questions, you look like a professional.
You look like someone who is ready for the job.
So, remember, prepare your stories and prepare your questions.
Now, let's talk about the
final piece of the puzzle.
The final thing is not about English.
It is about your mindset.
What do you do the night before the interview?
Many people stay
up late studying grammar.
This is a terrible idea.
You will be tired and stressed.
You should prepare your clothes.
Choose your shirt, your jacket,
your shoes.
If you look good, you feel good.
It's a simple trick, but it works.
Also, take a deep breath.
Do not try to learn new vocabulary at the last minute.
You already know the vocabulary you need.
Your goal is just to communicate.
Let's quickly review what we learned today.
One, stop trying to be perfect.
Be relaxed and friendly. Two, prepare short stories, not long speeches.
Three, four, tell me about yourself.
Give a short, professional introduction. Four,
ask good questions to the interviewer.
Five.
Prepare your clothes and relax the night before. That's it.
Five simple steps.
They are more important than grammar books.
They help you feel
confident.
And confidence is the most important thing. This method worked for my student.
He got the job.
I believe you can do it, too. Try this method today. And if this video helped you,
please leave a comment below.
Subscribe for more simple English tips. See you in the next one.
